predictions.description: The existing till software is named only as already in use. Vendor, version, whether it tracks stock today, and any sale-event or integration capability are absent, so the shared-view update requirement cannot be designed from the sources.
The owner wants a tool that tells booksellers what to offer, but no pricing rules, data sources, margins, condition factors, or lookup inputs are given.
Fair to us and fair to the customer permits materially different offer policies, from cost-recovery floors to customer-goodwill prices, with no operational definition.
Desired fairness of trade-in offers has no measurable success condition, threshold, or evaluation method.
Overrides must be recorded so the owner knows how often they happen, but no target rate, report grain, or success condition for that knowledge is stated.
Live before the Christmas season has no year, date, or definition of when that season starts.
Sources mix roughly thirty thousand titles with whether Chiado has a copy, so it is unclear whether the shared view is title presence, copy quantity, location-level availability, or something else.
Kept up to date when a sale happens could mean immediate, near-real-time, or end-of-day sync; latency and failure behavior are unspecified.

It is unclear whether the work is staff lookup only or also completes trade-ins, pays customers, adds acquired books to stock, handles transfers, returns, and new-versus-second-hand classification, or replaces the laminated price sheet.
Shared stock currency depends on the already-running till software, but that dependency is unresolved in identity, access, and behavior.
The request assumes sales on the current till can keep a shared stock view current; no evidence of APIs, exports, or stock capabilities is supplied.
Cross-shop availability after a till sale is an important property, but no test, audit, or proof obligation is stated.
Override recording is required, but no explicit way to prove completeness, identity of the bookseller, or captured before/after amounts is given.
A Christmas-season go-live is required while till integration, stock model, and trade-in method are unknown, leaving schedule risk uncontrolled.
New books must not be discounted under the stated Portuguese fixed-price rule; without classification and tool-boundary controls, a trade-in or stock tool could be applied to new books.
Three shops are claimed and Alfama and Chiado are named in an example; the third shop is not identified.
Roughly thirty thousand titles is the only inventory evidence; location-level quantities, condition, new versus second-hand split, and a system of record are not evidenced.
The chaotic laminated sheet is described as price lookup, while requested tools are shared stock and second-hand trade-in; whether the sheet is sale prices, trade-in offers, or both is unclear.
Record that they override does not specify whether to store actor, shop, book, suggested offer, final offer, reason, or only a count.
Booksellers work from shop iPads, but native versus browser, offline use, identity, and whether the till itself is in scope are unspecified.
